To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 2D micropunch shear model can predict the punch shear strength distribution and micromechanical punch shear damage mechanisms of unidirectional S-glass composites.

a simplified micromechanics model incorporating Weibul fiber strength distribution can simulate the punch-shear behavior of UD composite ribbons incorporating mixed mode fiber failure and fiber-matrix debonding mechanisms.

a simplified micromechanical model of punch shear in unidirectionally reinforced composites can be developed to predict the micromechanics of damage and the statistical distribution in the punch shear strength of a composite ribbon.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new punch shear experimental technique for the micromechanically based characterization of unidirectional composite laminates and the development of a simplified 2D stochastic micromechanical model for the simulation of punch shear damage behavior.
the development of an experimental and micromechanical approach to model the progressive damage behavior of uniaxially loaded unidirectional fiber reinforced composite ribbons.

the development and validation of a new stochastic micromechanical model for the prediction of the non-linear progressive punch shearing of unidirectional S-glass/DER353 epoxy composites at sub-millimetre length scale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents a combined approach of experimental and computational methods in simulating the statistical distribution of the non-linear progressive damage behavior of uniaxial fiber reinforced composites.
the proposed micromechanical model is capable to simulate the stochastic non-linear punch shear response of unidirectional S-glass/DER353 composites at micromechanical scales.
the micromechanically based stochastic finite element model can be used to simulate the progressive punch shear behavior and damage evolution of unidirectional fiber composites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stochastic micromechanical model developed in this study can predict the statistical distribution of the continuum punch shear behavior and micromechanical punch shear damage modes.

we have been successful in simulating the non-linear punch shear response of unidirectional composite ribbons incorporating the statistical distribution of the fiber strength and the fiber–matrix interface strength.

a stochastic finite element model of the punch shear problem can be used to characterize the micromechanic damage modes, and to simulate the statistical distribution of the continuum punch shear response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stochastic micromechanics approach can be applied to predict the non-linear damage behavior of uniaxial composites.
micromechanical models can be developed and correlated with punch shear experiments at the sub-millimeter level.
a simplified 2D finite element model can be used to model the punch shear behavior of a ribbon, incorporating the stochasticity of fiber failure and the fiber–matrix debonds.
